title: Wolves on the rise: rivalry shaking the Championship
seoTitle: Wolves on the rise: rivalry shaking the Championship
subtitle: The clash between Wolverhampton Wanderers and Birmingham City in the Championship reignites an old rivalry in English football.
excerpt: Wolverhampton Wanderers, known as Wolves, face Birmingham City in the Championship. Sunday's match revives an old rivalry, with the sides sitting ninth and tenth.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The term "wolves" is trending in searches, and the reason is the clash between Wolverhampton Wanderers, known as Wolves, and Birmingham City in the Championship. The teams renew their rivalry this Sunday in a game that promises to shake up the league table.

The Championship landscape

Wolverhampton Wanderers, currently in ninth place in the Championship with 8 points, face Birmingham City, which sits in tenth with 7 points. The match comes at a crucial moment for both clubs, who are looking to improve their positions on the table.

Birmingham City comes off a run of four unbeaten games in the Championship, with one win and three draws. This good form extends to nine unbeaten league games when the previous season is taken into account. The team earned four points in recent fixtures against Wrexham (2‑1 win) and Southampton (1‑1 draw), the latter a respectable point against a side chasing promotion. On the other hand, Wolverhampton Wanderers suffered a setback in 2026‑27, losing away to West Ham United, marking the first major disappointment of the season.

The rivalry on the pitch

After an eight‑year hiatus, Birmingham City and Wolverhampton Wanderers revive their rivalry. This game is highly anticipated, not only because of the proximity of the clubs in the table but also because of their historic encounters. The match is being played at St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park.

Team highlights

For Birmingham City, midfielder August Priske scored his first league goal of the season against Southampton after a cross from Patrick Roberts, who had a standout performance. New signing Liam Millar, arriving from Hull City, aims to impress on his debut for Birmingham, providing support and competition on the left flank. On the Wolves side, midfielder Fer Lopez has emerged as a key player, with two goals and two assists in his first four matches, showcasing the team’s offensive talent. Other players such as goalkeeper José Sá, defenders Jackson Tchatchoua and Nasser Djiga, and midfielder Marshall Munetsi are also expected to feature.

The Wolves' defence under scrutiny

Wolverhampton Wanderers’ defence has been a talking point. Former Birmingham midfielder Darren Carter noted a "vulnerability" in the Wolves’ back line despite the overall good performance of the side. According to former Wolves striker David Kelly, coach César Peixoto will need to work on improving the defensive unit, which appears to have a "season‑long problem" in terms of leadership at the rear. Incidents such as Phil Neumann’s headed clearance that hit the post and August Priske’s missed penalty illustrate the pressure on the Wolves’ defence.

Match moments

The game has been closely contested, with periods of pressure from both sides. A penalty appeal for Birmingham City was recorded when August Priske went down in the box after a challenge with Andre. Wolves’ goalkeeper José Sá made important saves from corners and distributed the ball forward, but was later brought down. Midfielder Marshall Munetsi received the first yellow card of the match after a foul on Patrick Roberts. Birmingham City also created chances, with Liam Millar trying to make an impact on his debut and Fer Lopez taking a free‑kick for the Wolves.
